text: COSTUME_SILLA_ELITE_A01 V02 (D-052, evidence-corrected): Silla senior elite observer, 5th to early 6th century, PROBABLE. ONE long-sleeved outer jacket-robe (jangyu) in muted grey-blue silk, hip-length or a little longer, with a STRAIGHT collar crossed SHALLOWLY right over left - no deep V, no wide open chest; only a thin line of the ivory hemp under-jacket shows at the collar. Sleeves are long and moderately wide, reaching the wrist. NO short-sleeved over-garment, NO layered short sleeve over long sleeve. No contrasting edging bands. Wide trousers gathered at the ankle; ankle boots over socks. Belt: a leather belt with a row of SILVER (or gilt-bronze) plaques and at most three short pendant drops - never gold plaques, never bronze or iron, never the long dangling Cheonmachong gold belt. Headwear: a LOW birch-bark cap with a blunt rounded top (gokkal shape), covered in plain silk, sitting close to the head - never a tall pointed cone, never a gold or gilt crown or gold cap ornament. Colours: grey-blue and ivory; never purple, never crimson. Forbidden: short sleeves, deep V crossover, gold crown, gold belt, bronze belt, tall pointed cap, Tang-style futou hat, round-collar danryeong, Joseon hanbok.
